name: Single-Arm Cable Lateral Raise
description: The single-arm cable lateral raise is a unilateral shoulder isolation exercise using a low-pulley cable. With the cable running across the body from the opposite side, constant tension is maintained on the lateral deltoid throughout the entire arc — including at the top where dumbbell lateral raises lose tension. This makes it mechanically superior for lateral deltoid isolation compared to free-weight raises.

execution.starting_position: Stand beside a low-pulley cable machine, holding the handle in the hand furthest from the machine (the cable crosses in front of the body). The working arm begins at the side, slightly in front of the hip.
execution.setup_instructions: Set the cable pulley to the lowest position and attach a single-handle D-ring. Stand perpendicular to the cable stack. Hold the handle in the hand on the opposite side from the machine.
steps: Step 1: Stand beside the cable machine, holding the handle in the far hand. Cable crosses in front of the body.
Step 2: Begin with the arm at the side, slightly in front of the hip. Slight elbow bend.
Step 3: Exhale and raise the arm upward and outward in a lateral arc to shoulder height.
Step 4: Pause briefly at the top, then inhale and lower the arm back to the start. Complete all reps, then switch sides.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as you raise; inhale as you lower.
common_mistakes: Shrugging the traps as the arm rises — consciously depress the shoulder during the raise
Raising too far above shoulder height into impingement range
safety_considerations: Stop the raise at or just above shoulder height unless mobility allows pain-free movement beyond
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Raise from hip/side to shoulder height; return controlled.
coaching_cues: Lead with the elbow, not the hand — keep the elbow slightly higher than the wrist
Think about pouring water from a jug at the top — slight internal rotation keeps the shoulder safe
